winner.title: Cambodian Fish Amok Recipe – an Authentic Steamed Fish Curry in the Old Style

evidence.authenticity: Traditional old-style recipe from an older generation of cooks; yellow kroeung, prahok, noni leaves under the filling, coconut-shell/banana-leaf/ramekin vessels, family-style serving; explains Khmer Empire/royal roots. Author is a travel food writer, not Khmer.
evidence.precision: Metric/volume amounts for 13 ingredients (500 g fish, 3 tbsp kroeung, 1/2 cup coconut milk); taste-test step (fry or microwave a spoonful) with flavor-balance cues; doneness cue 'firm to touch but still moist, not dry'; 20-30 min steam. No pan or steamer size; kroeung quantities are on a linked page.
evidence.testing: Explains the texture choice (chunky vs smooth by stirring), why to taste-test the raw mix, and what dryness means; rating 5 from 17 votes. No test kitchen.
evidence.photos: About 90 images on the page; stepImagesInSchema 0, so process photos not confirmed via WebFetch.
evidence.efficiency: Steps are sensible; kroeung must be made from a separate linked recipe; stated 60 min total is realistic.
evidence.access: Hard items (prahok, noni leaves, palm sugar, kaffir lime) all have substitutes given (shrimp paste, lime zest, brown sugar); noni leaves just omit-able.

winner.why: Most authentic, with a taste-test step and a clear doneness cue, beating Chef Nak's more precise but thinly explained version.

runnerUp.title: Cambodian Fish Amok

evidence.authenticity: Khmer author; snakehead, kroeung, banana-leaf cups with shiny sides out, Cambodian rice recommended.
evidence.precision: Grams for 7 of 11 ingredients, cube size 2-3 cm, leaf size 15 cm, fill 80%, steam 10+2 min; but kroeung amount is vague, no doneness cue for the steam, and the 'dried cubanelle pepper paste' is hard to source.
evidence.testing: Rest time given; little explanation of why.
evidence.photos: Only about 6 images on the page.
evidence.access: Kroeung and pepper paste not explained or substituted.

runnerUp.why: More precise measurements but weaker doneness cues, explanation and photos.

candidates.disqualified: Not traditional: cooked paste with peanuts and star anise, inspired by Rick Stein; Western adaptation
Loaded (200) but no Recipe structured data; not scored
